text:
A wise man lived in a small town. One day, a man ran up to him. “Teacher, I have something to tell you about your friend!” he said excitedly.

“Wait,” said the wise man. “Before you speak, let’s use the three questions. Is it true?”

The man thought. “Well... I heard it from someone. I’m not sure.”

“Is it good?” asked the wise man.

“No,” said the man. “It is bad news.”

“Is it useful?” asked the wise man. “Will it help me or my friend?”

The man was quiet. “No, I don’t think so.”

The wise man smiled. “If it is not true, not good, and not useful, why do you want to tell it to me?”

The man felt ashamed and went home. He understood that talking about other people can hurt them.

After that, he thought about these three questions before he spoke. And he never gossiped again. People in the town liked him more because he spoke only kind and useful words.

Moral: Before you speak, ask yourself: Is it true, is it kind, is it useful?
